lines.text: The Golden Fleece may be a sheepskin.
In legend, Jason sailed to Colchis to fetch a golden fleece.
About 2,000 years ago, Strabo wrote that Caucasus torrents carry gold.
lines.say: About two thousand years ago, Strabo wrote that Caucasus torrents carry gold.

lines.text: He said locals gather it with perforated troughs and fleecy skins.
Strabo added that this may be where the golden fleece myth began.
Appian, in the second century, described gold dust too fine to see.
Locals put shaggy sheepskins in the stream and collected the specks.
Appian wrote, Perhaps the golden fleece of Aetes was of this kind.
lines.say: Appian wrote, Perhaps the golden fleece of Ee tees was of this kind.

lines.text: People in Svaneti, Georgia, were long described panning rivers with sheepskins.
In 2014, geologists in Tbilisi argued the legend may rest on it.

post.caption: The Golden Fleece may be a sheepskin. In legend, Jason sailed to Colchis to fetch a golden fleece. About 2,000 years ago, Strabo wrote that Caucasus torrents carry gold. He said locals gather it with perforated troughs and fleecy skins. Strabo added that this may be where the golden fleece myth began. Appian, in the second century, described gold dust too fine to see. Locals put shaggy sheepskins in the stream and collected the specks. Appian wrote, Perhaps the golden fleece of Aetes was of this kind. People in Svaneti, Georgia, were long described panning rivers with sheepskins. In 2014, geologists in Tbilisi argued the legend may rest on it.
